171	        or params["r"] != _SCRYPT_R
172	        or params["p"] != _SCRYPT_P
173	        or len(params["salt"]) != 16
174	        or len(params["nonce"]) != _NONCE_LEN
175	    ):
176	        raise InvalidBundle("unsupported kdf parameters for field bundle")
177	    return params
178	
179	
180	def _require(data: dict, field: str, types) -> object:
181	    if field not in data or not isinstance(data[field], types):
182	        kind = "string" if types is str else "value"
183	        raise InvalidBundle("field %s must be a %s" % (field, kind))
184	    return data[field]
185	
186	
187	def validate_provider_block(block, where: str):
188	    """Validate an optional KMS/HSM provenance block on one version.
189	
190	    The block is ``{"provider_id", "handle", "encrypted_material"}``; every
191	    field must be a non-empty string. ``None``/absent is valid and means the
192	    version originated on the built-in local provider (``keymgr-export-v1``
193	    bundles emitted before the provider layer carry no such field). Returns
194	    the cleaned block or None for a legacy version.
195	    """
196	    if block is None:
197	        return None
198	    prefix = where + ".provider"
199	    if not isinstance(block, dict):
200	        raise InvalidBundle("field %s must be an object" % prefix)
201	    unknown = set(block) - {"provider_id", "handle", "encrypted_material"}
202	    if unknown:
203	        raise InvalidBundle(
204	            "unknown field %s.%s" % (prefix, sorted(unknown)[0])
205	        )
206	    clean = {}
207	    for name in ("provider_id", "handle", "encrypted_material"):
208	        value = block.get(name)
209	        if not isinstance(value, str) or not value:
210	            raise InvalidBundle(
211	                "field %s.%s must be a non-empty string" % (prefix, name)
212	            )
213	        clean[name] = value
214	    return clean
215	
216	
217	def validate_version(ver, where: str) -> dict:
218	    """Validate one versions[i] block; ``where`` names it in error messages."""
219	    if not isinstance(ver, dict):
220	        raise InvalidBundle("field %s must be an object" % where)
221	    number = ver.get("version")
222	    created_at = ver.get("created_at")
223	    algorithm = ver.get("algorithm")
224	    public_key = ver.get("public_key")
225	    private_material = ver.get("private_material")
226	    if not isinstance(number, int) or isinstance(number, bool) or number < 1:
227	        raise InvalidBundle(
228	            "field %s.version must be a positive integer" % where
229	        )
230	    if not isinstance(created_at, str) or not created_at:
231	        raise InvalidBundle("field %s.created_at must be a string" % where)
232	    if algorithm not in SUPPORTED_ALGORITHMS:
233	        raise InvalidBundle(
234	            "field %s.algorithm must be one of: %s"
235	            % (where, ", ".join(SUPPORTED_ALGORITHMS))
236	        )
237	    if public_key is not None and not isinstance(public_key, str):
238	        raise InvalidBundle(
239	            "field %s.public_key must be a string or null" % where
240	        )
241	    if not isinstance(private_material, str) or not private_material:
242	        raise InvalidBundle(
243	            "field %s.private_material must be a non-empty string" % where
244	        )
245	    provider = validate_provider_block(ver.get("provider"), where)
246	    return {
247	        "version": number,
248	        "created_at": created_at,
249	        "algorithm": algorithm,
250	        "public_key": public_key,
251	        "private_material": private_material,
252	        "provider": provider,
253	    }
254	
255	
256	def validate_revocation_fields(data: dict, where: str = "") -> dict:
257	    """Validate status/reason/operator/revoked_at and return them cleaned."""
258	    prefix = where + "." if where else ""
259	    status = _require(data, "status", str)
260	    if status not in ("active", "revoked"):
261	        raise InvalidBundle(
262	            "field %sstatus must be 'active' or 'revoked'" % prefix
263	        )
264	    reason = data.get("reason")
265	    operator = data.get("operator")
266	    revoked_at = data.get("revoked_at")
267	    if status == "revoked":
268	        for name, value in (
269	            ("reason", reason),
270	            ("operator", operator),
271	            ("revoked_at", revoked_at),
272	        ):
273	            if not isinstance(value, str) or not value:
274	                raise InvalidBundle(
275	                    "field %s%s must be a non-empty string for a revoked key"
276	                    % (prefix, name)
277	                )
278	    elif any(v is not None for v in (reason, operator, revoked_at)):
279	        raise InvalidBundle(
280	            "revocation fields must be null for an active key"
281	        )
282	    return {
283	        "status": status,
284	        "reason": reason,
285	        "operator": operator,
286	        "revoked_at": revoked_at,
287	    }
288	
289	
290	def validate_payload(data: dict) -> dict:
291	    """Validate the decrypted export payload and return a cleaned copy.
292	
293	    Raises InvalidBundle naming the offending field on any structural
294	    problem or missing field.
295	    """
296	    if not isinstance(data, dict):
297	        raise InvalidBundle("bundle payload must be a JSON object")
298	    if data.get("format") != FORMAT:
299	        raise InvalidBundle("field format must be %r" % FORMAT)
300	
301	    key_id = _require(data, "key_id", str)
302	    from .store import is_valid_key_id
303	
304	    if not is_valid_key_id(key_id):
305	        raise InvalidBundle("field key_id must be a UUID4")
306	    label = _require(data, "label", str)
307	
308	    versions = data.get("versions")
309	    if not isinstance(versions, list) or not versions:
310	        raise InvalidBundle("field versions must be a non-empty array")
311	
312	    seen_versions = set()
313	    clean_versions = []
314	    for index, ver in enumerate(versions):
315	        where = "versions[%d]" % index
316	        clean = validate_version(ver, where)
317	        if clean["version"] in seen_versions:
318	            raise InvalidBundle(
319	                "field %s.version duplicates another version" % where
320	            )
321	        seen_versions.add(clean["version"])
322	        clean_versions.append(clean)
323	
324	    current_version = data.get("current_version")
325	    expected_numbers = set(range(1, len(seen_versions) + 1))
326	    if seen_versions != expected_numbers:
327	        raise InvalidBundle(
328	            "field versions must be the contiguous sequence 1..N with no gaps"
329	        )
330	    if (
331	        not isinstance(current_version, int)
332	        or isinstance(current_version, bool)
333	        or current_version != len(clean_versions)
334	    ):
335	        raise InvalidBundle(
336	            "field current_version must point at the latest exported version"
337	        )
338	    clean_versions.sort(key=lambda v: v["version"])
339	
340	    revocation = validate_revocation_fields(data)
341	
342	    return {
343	        "format": FORMAT,
344	        "key_id": key_id,
345	        "label": label,
346	        "current_version": current_version,
347	        "reason": revocation["reason"],
348	        "operator": revocation["operator"],
349	        "revoked_at": revocation["revoked_at"],
350	        "status": revocation["status"],
351	        "versions": clean_versions,
352	    }
353	
354	
355	def decode_bundle(bundle: str, passphrase: str) -> dict:
356	    """Decrypt and validate a bundle.
357	
358	    Raises WrongPassphrase for authentication failures (wrong passphrase or
359	    tampered ciphertext) and InvalidBundle for structural, format/version and
360	    missing-field problems.
361	    """
362	    plaintext = open_envelope(bundle, passphrase, FORMAT)
363	    try:
364	        data = json.loads(plaintext.decode("utf-8"))
365	    except (ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError) as exc:
366	        raise InvalidBundle("bundle payload is not valid JSON") from exc
367	    return validate_payload(data)
368

1	"""Persistent append-only audit ledger with tenant-isolated pagination."""
2	
3	import base64
4	import hashlib
5	import hmac
6	import json
7	import os
8	import threading
9	import uuid
10	from dataclasses import dataclass
11	from typing import List, NamedTuple, Optional
12	
13	try:  # fcntl is POSIX-only.
14	    import fcntl
15	except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover - non-POSIX platforms
16	    fcntl = None
17	
18	# Actions written to the ledger. A request with a missing, empty, illegal or
19	# tenant-inconsistent identifier is recorded as TENANT_CONFLICT instead.
20	ACTION_CREATE = "create"
21	ACTION_READ = "read"
22	ACTION_ROTATE = "rotate"
23	ACTION_BATCH_ROTATE = "batch_rotate"
24	ACTION_REVOKE = "revoke"
25	ACTION_IMPORT = "import"
26	ACTION_EXPORT = "export"
27	ACTION_AUDIT = "audit"
28	ACTION_TENANT_CONFLICT = "tenant_conflict"
29	# Policy management actions. These are audited but are never themselves
30	# governed by a tenant policy (management is exempt from enforcement).
31	ACTION_POLICY_READ = "policy_read"
32	ACTION_POLICY_UPDATE = "policy_update"
33	ACTION_POLICY_DELETE = "policy_delete"
34	ACTIONS = (
35	    ACTION_CREATE,
36	    ACTION_READ,
37	    ACTION_ROTATE,
38	    ACTION_BATCH_ROTATE,
39	    ACTION_REVOKE,
40	    ACTION_IMPORT,
41	    ACTION_EXPORT,
42	    ACTION_AUDIT,
43	    ACTION_TENANT_CONFLICT,
44	    ACTION_POLICY_READ,
45	    ACTION_POLICY_UPDATE,
46	    ACTION_POLICY_DELETE,
47	)
48	
49	OUTCOME_SUCCESS = "success"
50	OUTCOME_REJECTED = "rejected"
51	OUTCOMES = (OUTCOME_SUCCESS, OUTCOME_REJECTED)
52	
53	_LOG_NAME = "audit.log"
54	_LOCK_NAME = "audit.log.lock"
55	_SECRET_NAME = "audit.secret"
56	
57	
58	class LedgerError(Exception):
59	    """Raised when the audit ledger cannot be written or read durably."""
60	
61	
62	class InvalidCursor(Exception):
63	    """Raised when a pagination cursor is malformed, tampered or stale."""
64	
65	
66	@dataclass
67	class AuditEvent:
68	    """One immutable audit record. Never carries key material."""
69	
70	    event_id: str
71	    tenant_id: Optional[str]
72	    action: str
73	    key_id: Optional[str]
74	    outcome: str
75	    timestamp: str
76	    seq: int = 0
77	
78	    def to_json(self) -> dict:
79	        """Serialize to a plain dict suitable for JSON storage."""
80	        return {
81	            "event_id": self.event_id,
82	            "tenant_id": self.tenant_id,
83	            "action": self.action,
84	            "key_id": self.key_id,
85	            "outcome": self.outcome,
86	            "timestamp": self.timestamp,
87	            "seq": self.seq,
88	        }
89	
90	    @classmethod
91	    def from_json(cls, data: dict) -> "AuditEvent":
92	        return cls(
93	            event_id=data["event_id"],
94	            tenant_id=data.get("tenant_id"),
95	            action=data["action"],
96	            key_id=data.get("key_id"),
97	            outcome=data["outcome"],
98	            timestamp=data["timestamp"],
99	            seq=int(data.get("seq", 0)),
100	        )
101	
102	    def to_response(self) -> dict:
103	        """Projection for GET /v1/audit: ledger-internal seq is omitted."""
104	        return {
105	            "event_id": self.event_id,
106	            "tenant_id": self.tenant_id,
107	            "action": self.action,
108	            "key_id": self.key_id,
109	            "outcome": self.outcome,
110	            "timestamp": self.timestamp,
111	        }
112	
113	
114	class AuditPage(NamedTuple):
115	    """Result of one ledger query: a page of events and the next cursor."""
116	
117	    events: List[AuditEvent]
118	    next_cursor: Optional[str]
119	
120	
121	class AuditLog:
122	    """File-backed append-only audit log (one JSON object per line).
123	
124	    All appends are serialized by one process-wide lock plus an exclusive
125	    ``fcntl`` lock on a sidecar file, so multiple server threads and processes
126	    share a monotonic ``seq`` without interleaving or losing lines. Pagination
127	    cursors are HMAC-signed and bound to the tenant, the active filters and the
128	    ledger snapshot they were issued against.
129	    """
130	
131	    def __init__(self, data_dir: str) -> None:
132	        self.data_dir = data_dir
133	        os.makedirs(self.data_dir, exist_ok=True)
134	        self._log_path = os.path.join(data_dir, _LOG_NAME)
135	        self._lock_path = os.path.join(data_dir, _LOCK_NAME)
136	        self._secret_path = os.path.join(data_dir, _SECRET_NAME)
137	        self._append_lock = threading.Lock()
138	        self._secret: Optional[bytes] = None
139	
140	    # -- paths / locking ---------------------------------------------------
141	    @property
142	    def path(self) -> str:
143	        return self._log_path
144	
145	    def _locked_file(self):
146	        """Open the sidecar lock file and take an exclusive fcntl lock."""
147	        fd = os.open(self._lock_path, os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT, 0o600)
148	        if fcntl is None:  # pragma: no cover - non-POSIX platforms
149	            return fd
150	        try:
151	            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
152	        except OSError:
153	            os.close(fd)
154	            raise
155	        return fd
156	
157	    def _unlock_file(self, fd: int) -> None:
158	        try:
159	            if fcntl is not None:  # pragma: no branch - POSIX in practice
160	                fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
161	        finally:
162	            os.close(fd)
163	
164	    def _signing_secret(self) -> bytes:
165	        """Load (creating once, 0600) the HMAC secret used for cursors.
166	
167	        The read-or-create runs under the same cross-process file lock as
168	        appends, so two processes initializing concurrently cannot raise
169	        FileExistsError or read a half-written secret.
170	        """
171	        if self._secret is not None:
172	            return self._secret
173	        try:
174	            with open(self._secret_path, "rb") as fh:
175	                secret = fh.read()
176	            if secret:
177	                self._secret = secret
178	                return secret
179	        except FileNotFoundError:
180	            pass
181	        fd = self._locked_file()
182	        try:
183	            # Re-check under the lock: another process may have completed
184	            # the initialization while this one waited.
185	            try:
186	                with open(self._secret_path, "rb") as fh:
187	                    secret = fh.read()
188	                if secret:
189	                    self._secret = secret
190	                    return secret
191	            except FileNotFoundError:
192	                pass
193	            secret = os.urandom(32).hex().encode("ascii")
194	            out = os.open(
195	                self._secret_path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_TRUNC, 0o600
196	            )
197	            try:
198	                os.write(out, secret)
199	                os.fsync(out)
200	            finally:
201	                os.close(out)
202	            self._secret = secret
203	            return secret
204	        finally:
205	            self._unlock_file(fd)
206	
207	    # -- reads -------------------------------------------------------------
208	    def _read_all_locked(self) -> List[AuditEvent]:
209	        """Read every ledger line. Caller must hold no lock; takes none."""
210	        try:
211	            with open(self._log_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
212	                lines = fh.readlines()
213	        except FileNotFoundError:
214	            return []
215	        except OSError as exc:
216	            raise LedgerError("cannot read audit log: %s" % exc) from exc
217	        events: List[AuditEvent] = []
218	        for line in lines:
219	            line = line.strip()
220	            if not line:
221	                continue
222	            try:
223	                events.append(AuditEvent.from_json(json.loads(line)))
224	            except (ValueError, KeyError, TypeError):
225	                # A torn/corrupt tail line must not poison reads; the writer
226	                # only ever fsyncs complete lines.
227	                continue
228	        return events
229	
230	    def _read_all(self) -> List[AuditEvent]:
231	        """Read under both locks for a consistent cross-process snapshot.
232	
233	        Appends commit (write + fsync) while holding the exclusive file
234	        lock, so a reader holding the same lock never observes a torn or
235	        partially-committed tail.
236	        """
237	        with self._append_lock:
238	            fd = self._locked_file()
239	            try:
240	                return self._read_all_locked()
241	            finally:
242	                self._unlock_file(fd)
243	
244	    @staticmethod
245	    def _fingerprint(events: List[AuditEvent]) -> str:
246	        """Stable digest identifying one ledger snapshot (its event set)."""
247	        digest = hashlib.sha256()
248	        for event in events:
249	            digest.update(str(event.seq).encode("ascii"))
250	            digest.update(b":")
251	            digest.update(event.event_id.encode("utf-8"))
252	            digest.update(b"\n")
253	        digest.update(b"count=%d" % len(events))
254	        return digest.hexdigest()
255	
256	    # -- writes ------------------------------------------------------------
257	    def new_event(
258	        self,
259	        tenant_id: Optional[str],
260	        action: str,
261	        key_id: Optional[str],
262	        outcome: str,
263	        timestamp: Optional[str] = None,
264	        event_id: Optional[str] = None,
265	    ) -> AuditEvent:
266	        """Mint an event with a fresh (or supplied) id and UTC timestamp.
267	
268	        ``event_id`` may be supplied so an idempotent operation's audit event
269	        is named after its ``operation_id``; crash recovery then resolves both
270	        by the same identifier. The ledger dedupes on event_id, so reusing an
271	        id never appends twice.
272	        """
273	        # Imported lazily to avoid a module import cycle at package import.
274	        from datetime import datetime, timezone
275	
276	        return AuditEvent(
277	            event_id=event_id or str(uuid.uuid4()),
278	            tenant_id=tenant_id,
279	            action=action,
280	            key_id=key_id,
281	            outcome=outcome,
282	            timestamp=timestamp
283	            or datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
284	        )
285	
286	    def append(self, event: AuditEvent) -> AuditEvent:
287	        """Append one event durably, assigning the next monotonic seq.
288	
289	        Raises LedgerError if the line cannot be committed. The fsync before
290	        release means a returned event is on disk.
291	        """
292	        with self._append_lock:
293	            fd = self._locked_file()
294	            try:
295	                existing = self._read_all_locked()
296	                # Idempotent on event_id: recovery re-append after a crash
297	                # between the ledger write and the outbox-marker clear must
298	                # not produce a duplicate line.
299	                for prior in existing:
300	                    if prior.event_id == event.event_id:
301	                        event.seq = prior.seq
302	                        return event
303	                event.seq = (existing[-1].seq + 1) if existing else 1
304	                line = json.dumps(event.to_json(), separators=(",", ":")) + "\n"
305	                try:
306	                    with open(self._log_path, "a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
307	                        fh.write(line)
308	                        fh.flush()
309	                        os.fsync(fh.fileno())
310	                except OSError as exc:
311	                    raise LedgerError("cannot write audit log: %s" % exc) from exc
312	            finally:
313	                self._unlock_file(fd)
314	        return event
315	
316	    def get_event(self, event_id: str) -> Optional[AuditEvent]:
317	        """Look up one event by event_id, or None if it has not been logged.
318	
319	        Used by multi-file restore recovery to decide whether the shared
320	        event reached the ledger after a crash.
321	        """
322	        for event in self._read_all():
323	            if event.event_id == event_id:
324	                return event
325	        return None
326	
327	    # -- cursors -----------------------------------------------------------
328	    def _encode_cursor(self, payload: dict) -> str:
329	        raw = json.dumps(payload, separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True).encode("utf-8")
330	        token = base64.urlsafe_b64encode(raw).rstrip(b"=")
331	        mac = hmac.new(self._signing_secret(), token, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
332	        return (token + b"." + mac.encode("ascii")).decode("ascii")
333	
334	    def _decode_cursor(self, raw: str) -> dict:
335	        try:
336	            token_b, mac_b = raw.encode("ascii").split(b".", 1)
337	        except (ValueError, AttributeError) as exc:
338	            raise InvalidCursor("malformed cursor") from exc
339	        expected = hmac.new(
340	            self._signing_secret(), token_b, hashlib.sha256
341	        ).hexdigest().encode("ascii")
342	        if not hmac.compare_digest(expected, mac_b):
343	            raise InvalidCursor("invalid or tampered cursor")
344	        padded = token_b + b"=" * (-len(token_b) % 4)
345	        try:
346	            payload = json.loads(base64.urlsafe_b64decode(padded).decode("utf-8"))
347	        except (ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError) as exc:
348	            raise InvalidCursor("malformed cursor") from exc
349	        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
350	            raise InvalidCursor("malformed cursor")
351	        return payload
352	
353	    # -- queries -----------------------------------------------------------
354	    @staticmethod
355	    def _sort_key(event: AuditEvent):
356	        return event.timestamp, event.event_id, event.seq
357	
358	    def query(
359	        self,
360	        tenant_id: str,
361	        key_id: Optional[str] = None,
362	        action: Optional[str] = None,
363	        limit: int = 100,
364	        cursor: Optional[str] = None,
365	    ) -> AuditPage:
366	        """Return one tenant-isolated, filter-bound, snapshot-bound page.
367	
368	        Events are ordered by (timestamp, event_id) ascending. Conflict
369	        records carry a null tenant and are therefore visible to nobody.
370	        A cursor is valid only with the same tenant, filters and an unchanged
371	        ledger snapshot; otherwise InvalidCursor is raised.
372	        """
373	        anchor = None
374	        fingerprint = None
375	        if cursor is not None:
376	            payload = self._decode_cursor(cursor)
377	            try:
378	                if payload.get("t") != tenant_id:
379	                    raise InvalidCursor("cursor does not match tenant_id")
380	                if payload.get("k") != key_id or payload.get("a") != action:
381	                    raise InvalidCursor("cursor does not match filters")
382	                if int(payload.get("l", -1)) != limit:
383	                    raise InvalidCursor("cursor does not match limit")
384	                anchor = (payload["ts"], payload["eid"], int(payload["seq"]))
385	                fingerprint = payload["f"]
386	            except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
387	                raise InvalidCursor("malformed cursor") from exc
388	
389	        events = self._read_all()
390	
391	        selected_all = [
392	            e
393	            for e in events
394	            if e.tenant_id == tenant_id
395	            and (key_id is None or e.key_id == key_id)
396	            and (action is None or e.action == action)
397	        ]
398	        selected_all.sort(key=self._sort_key)
399	        # The snapshot is scoped to exactly the events this tenant and these
400	        # filters can see: another tenant's activity must not invalidate the
401	        # cursor, while any change to the visible set does.
402	        current_fingerprint = self._fingerprint(selected_all)
403	        if fingerprint is not None and fingerprint != current_fingerprint:
404	            raise InvalidCursor("cursor snapshot is no longer valid")
405	
406	        selected = selected_all
407	        if anchor is not None:
408	            selected = [e for e in selected if self._sort_key(e) > anchor]
409	
410	        page = selected[:limit]
411	        if len(selected) > limit and page:
412	            last = page[-1]
413	            next_cursor = self._encode_cursor(
414	                {
415	                    "v": 1,
416	                    "t": tenant_id,
417	                    "k": key_id,
418	                    "a": action,
419	                    "l": limit,
420	                    "ts": last.timestamp,
421	                    "eid": last.event_id,
422	                    "seq": last.seq,
423	                    "f": current_fingerprint,
424	                }
425	            )
426	        else:
427	            next_cursor = None
428	        return AuditPage(events=page, next_cursor=next_cursor)

"""Persistent append-only audit ledger with tenant-isolated pagination."""

class LedgerError(Exception):
    """Raised when the audit ledger cannot be written or read durably."""


class InvalidCursor(Exception):
    """Raised when a pagination cursor is malformed, tampered or stale."""


@dataclass
class AuditEvent:
    """One immutable audit record. Never carries key material."""

    event_id: str
    tenant_id: Optional[str]
    action: str
    key_id: Optional[str]
    outcome: str
    timestamp: str
    seq: int = 0

    def to_json(self) -> dict:
        """Serialize to a plain dict suitable for JSON storage."""
        return {
            "event_id": self.event_id,
            "tenant_id": self.tenant_id,
            "action": self.action,
            "key_id": self.key_id,
            "outcome": self.outcome,
            "timestamp": self.timestamp,
            "seq": self.seq,
        }

    @classmethod
    def from_json(cls, data: dict) -> "AuditEvent":
        return cls(
            event_id=data["event_id"],
            tenant_id=data.get("tenant_id"),
            action=data["action"],
            key_id=data.get("key_id"),
            outcome=data["outcome"],
            timestamp=data["timestamp"],
            seq=int(data.get("seq", 0)),
        )

    def to_response(self) -> dict:
        """Projection for GET /v1/audit: ledger-internal seq is omitted."""
        return {
            "event_id": self.event_id,
            "tenant_id": self.tenant_id,
            "action": self.action,
            "key_id": self.key_id,
            "outcome": self.outcome,
            "timestamp": self.timestamp,
        }


class AuditPage(NamedTuple):
    """Result of one ledger query: a page of events and the next cursor."""

    events: List[AuditEvent]
    next_cursor: Optional[str]


class AuditLog:
    """File-backed append-only audit log (one JSON object per line).

    All appends are serialized by one process-wide lock plus an exclusive
    ``fcntl`` lock on a sidecar file, so multiple server threads and processes
    share a monotonic ``seq`` without interleaving or losing lines. Pagination
    cursors are HMAC-signed and bound to the tenant, the active filters and the
    ledger snapshot they were issued against.
    """

    def __init__(self, data_dir: str) -> None:
        self.data_dir = data_dir
        os.makedirs(self.data_dir, exist_ok=True)
        self._log_path = os.path.join(data_dir, _LOG_NAME)
        self._lock_path = os.path.join(data_dir, _LOCK_NAME)
        self._secret_path = os.path.join(data_dir, _SECRET_NAME)
        self._append_lock = threading.Lock()
        self._secret: Optional[bytes] = None

    # -- paths / locking ---------------------------------------------------
    @property
    def path(self) -> str:
        return self._log_path

    def _locked_file(self):
        """Open the sidecar lock file and take an exclusive fcntl lock."""
        fd = os.open(self._lock_path, os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT, 0o600)
        if fcntl is None:  # pragma: no cover - non-POSIX platforms
            return fd
        try:
            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
        except OSError:
            os.close(fd)
            raise
        return fd

    def _unlock_file(self, fd: int) -> None:
        try:
            if fcntl is not None:  # pragma: no branch - POSIX in practice
                fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
        finally:
            os.close(fd)

    def _signing_secret(self) -> bytes:
        """Load (creating once, 0600) the HMAC secret used for cursors.

        The read-or-create runs under the same cross-process file lock as
        appends, so two processes initializing concurrently cannot raise
        FileExistsError or read a half-written secret.
        """
        if self._secret is not None:
            return self._secret
        try:
            with open(self._secret_path, "rb") as fh:
                secret = fh.read()
            if secret:
                self._secret = secret
                return secret
        except FileNotFoundError:
            pass
        fd = self._locked_file()
        try:
            # Re-check under the lock: another process may have completed
            # the initialization while this one waited.
            try:
                with open(self._secret_path, "rb") as fh:
                    secret = fh.read()
                if secret:
                    self._secret = secret
                    return secret
            except FileNotFoundError:
                pass
            secret = os.urandom(32).hex().encode("ascii")
            out = os.open(
                self._secret_path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_TRUNC, 0o600
            )
            try:
                os.write(out, secret)
                os.fsync(out)
            finally:
                os.close(out)
            self._secret = secret
            return secret
        finally:
            self._unlock_file(fd)

    # -- reads -------------------------------------------------------------
    def _read_all_locked(self) -> List[AuditEvent]:
        """Read every ledger line. Caller must hold no lock; takes none."""
        try:
            with open(self._log_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
                lines = fh.readlines()
        except FileNotFoundError:
            return []
        except OSError as exc:
            raise LedgerError("cannot read audit log: %s" % exc) from exc
        events: List[AuditEvent] = []
        for line in lines:
            line = line.strip()
            if not line:
                continue
            try:
                events.append(AuditEvent.from_json(json.loads(line)))
            except (ValueError, KeyError, TypeError):
                # A torn/corrupt tail line must not poison reads; the writer
                # only ever fsyncs complete lines.
                continue
        return events

    def _read_all(self) -> List[AuditEvent]:
        """Read under both locks for a consistent cross-process snapshot.

        Appends commit (write + fsync) while holding the exclusive file
        lock, so a reader holding the same lock never observes a torn or
        partially-committed tail.
        """
        with self._append_lock:
            fd = self._locked_file()
            try:
                return self._read_all_locked()
            finally:
                self._unlock_file(fd)

    @staticmethod
    def _fingerprint(events: List[AuditEvent]) -> str:
        """Stable digest identifying one ledger snapshot (its event set)."""
        digest = hashlib.sha256()
        for event in events:
            digest.update(str(event.seq).encode("ascii"))
            digest.update(b":")
            digest.update(event.event_id.encode("utf-8"))
            digest.update(b"\n")
        digest.update(b"count=%d" % len(events))
        return digest.hexdigest()

    # -- writes ------------------------------------------------------------
    def new_event(
        self,
        tenant_id: Optional[str],
        action: str,
        key_id: Optional[str],
        outcome: str,
        timestamp: Optional[str] = None,
        event_id: Optional[str] = None,
    ) -> AuditEvent:
        """Mint an event with a fresh (or supplied) id and UTC timestamp.

        ``event_id`` may be supplied so an idempotent operation's audit event
        is named after its ``operation_id``; crash recovery then resolves both
        by the same identifier. The ledger dedupes on event_id, so reusing an
        id never appends twice.
        """
        # Imported lazily to avoid a module import cycle at package import.
        from datetime import datetime, timezone

        return AuditEvent(
            event_id=event_id or str(uuid.uuid4()),
            tenant_id=tenant_id,
            action=action,
            key_id=key_id,
            outcome=outcome,
            timestamp=timestamp
            or datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
        )

    def append(self, event: AuditEvent) -> AuditEvent:
        """Append one event durably, assigning the next monotonic seq.

        Raises LedgerError if the line cannot be committed. The fsync before
        release means a returned event is on disk.
        """
        with self._append_lock:
            fd = self._locked_file()
            try:
                existing = self._read_all_locked()
                # Idempotent on event_id: recovery re-append after a crash
                # between the ledger write and the outbox-marker clear must
                # not produce a duplicate line.
                for prior in existing:
                    if prior.event_id == event.event_id:
                        event.seq = prior.seq
                        return event
                event.seq = (existing[-1].seq + 1) if existing else 1
                line = json.dumps(event.to_json(), separators=(",", ":")) + "\n"
                try:
                    with open(self._log_path, "a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
                        fh.write(line)
                        fh.flush()
                        os.fsync(fh.fileno())
                except OSError as exc:
                    raise LedgerError("cannot write audit log: %s" % exc) from exc
            finally:
                self._unlock_file(fd)
        return event

    def get_event(self, event_id: str) -> Optional[AuditEvent]:
        """Look up one event by event_id, or None if it has not been logged.

        Used by multi-file restore recovery to decide whether the shared
        event reached the ledger after a crash.
        """
        for event in self._read_all():
            if event.event_id == event_id:
                return event
        return None

    # -- cursors -----------------------------------------------------------
    def _encode_cursor(self, payload: dict) -> str:
        raw = json.dumps(payload, separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True).encode("utf-8")
        token = base64.urlsafe_b64encode(raw).rstrip(b"=")
        mac = hmac.new(self._signing_secret(), token, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
        return (token + b"." + mac.encode("ascii")).decode("ascii")

    def _decode_cursor(self, raw: str) -> dict:
        try:
            token_b, mac_b = raw.encode("ascii").split(b".", 1)
        except (ValueError, AttributeError) as exc:
            raise InvalidCursor("malformed cursor") from exc
        expected = hmac.new(
            self._signing_secret(), token_b, hashlib.sha256
        ).hexdigest().encode("ascii")
        if not hmac.compare_digest(expected, mac_b):
            raise InvalidCursor("invalid or tampered cursor")
        padded = token_b + b"=" * (-len(token_b) % 4)
        try:
            payload = json.loads(base64.urlsafe_b64decode(padded).decode("utf-8"))
        except (ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError) as exc:
            raise InvalidCursor("malformed cursor") from exc
        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
            raise InvalidCursor("malformed cursor")
        return payload

    # -- queries -----------------------------------------------------------
    @staticmethod
    def _sort_key(event: AuditEvent):
        return event.timestamp, event.event_id, event.seq

    def query(
        self,
        tenant_id: str,
        key_id: Optional[str] = None,
        action: Optional[str] = None,
        limit: int = 100,
        cursor: Optional[str] = None,
    ) -> AuditPage:
        """Return one tenant-isolated, filter-bound, snapshot-bound page.

        Events are ordered by (timestamp, event_id) ascending. Conflict
        records carry a null tenant and are therefore visible to nobody.
        A cursor is valid only with the same tenant, filters and an unchanged
        ledger snapshot; otherwise InvalidCursor is raised.
        """
        anchor = None
        fingerprint = None
        if cursor is not None:
            payload = self._decode_cursor(cursor)
            try:
                if payload.get("t") != tenant_id:
                    raise InvalidCursor("cursor does not match tenant_id")
                if payload.get("k") != key_id or payload.get("a") != action:
                    raise InvalidCursor("cursor does not match filters")
                if int(payload.get("l", -1)) != limit:
                    raise InvalidCursor("cursor does not match limit")
                anchor = (payload["ts"], payload["eid"], int(payload["seq"]))
                fingerprint = payload["f"]
            except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
                raise InvalidCursor("malformed cursor") from exc

        events = self._read_all()

        selected_all = [
            e
            for e in events
            if e.tenant_id == tenant_id
            and (key_id is None or e.key_id == key_id)
            and (action is None or e.action == action)
        ]
        selected_all.sort(key=self._sort_key)
        # The snapshot is scoped to exactly the events this tenant and these
        # filters can see: another tenant's activity must not invalidate the
        # cursor, while any change to the visible set does.
        current_fingerprint = self._fingerprint(selected_all)
        if fingerprint is not None and fingerprint != current_fingerprint:
            raise InvalidCursor("cursor snapshot is no longer valid")

        selected = selected_all
        if anchor is not None:
            selected = [e for e in selected if self._sort_key(e) > anchor]

        page = selected[:limit]
        if len(selected) > limit and page:
            last = page[-1]
            next_cursor = self._encode_cursor(
                {
                    "v": 1,
                    "t": tenant_id,
                    "k": key_id,
                    "a": action,
                    "l": limit,
                    "ts": last.timestamp,
                    "eid": last.event_id,
                    "seq": last.seq,
                    "f": current_fingerprint,
                }
            )
        else:
            next_cursor = None
        return AuditPage(events=page, next_cursor=next_cursor)

2	
3	A policy document is a list of rules; each rule binds a ``subject`` (the
4	X-Operator-Id of the caller), a set of ``actions`` and an ``effect`` of
5	``allow`` or ``deny``. Enforcement, for one (tenant, subject, action):
6	
7	* a tenant with no document is unrestricted (every action is allowed);
8	* among the rules whose subject equals the caller and whose actions contain
9	  the action, any ``deny`` wins over ``allow``;
10	* if no matching rule exists the action is denied (default deny).

13	outbox transaction as key records: the file first lands carrying the audit

260	        """Commit outbox events left pending by a crashed process."""
261	        try:
262	            names = os.listdir(self.dir_path)
263	        except OSError:
264	            return
265	        for name in names:
266	            if not name.endswith(".json") and not name.endswith(".json.del"):
267	                continue
268	            path = os.path.join(self.dir_path, name)
269	            doc = self._read_doc(path)
270	            if doc is None:
271	                continue
272	            tenant_id, rules, pending_event = doc
273	            if not pending_event:
274	                # A tombstone left behind after a successful ledger append:
275	                # finish the delete.
276	                if name.endswith(".del"):
277	                    try:
278	                        os.unlink(path)
279	                    except OSError:
280	                        pass
281	                continue
282	            # A multi-file tenant restore transaction is resolved by the
283	            # RestoreCoordinator (its manifest drives the shared event).
284	            if isinstance(pending_event, dict) and pending_event.get("_restore"):
285	                continue
286	            event = AuditEvent.from_json(pending_event)
287	            if name.endswith(".json.del"):                # A delete tombstone. If the original file is still on disk the
288	                # crash happened before the unlink, so the delete never
289	                # happened: discard the tombstone without appending. Otherwise
290	                # finish the transaction (append is idempotent on event_id).
291	                original = path[: -len(".del")]
292	                if os.path.exists(original):
293	                    try:
294	                        os.unlink(path)
295	                    except OSError:
296	                        pass
297	                    continue
298	                self.audit.append(event)
299	                try:
300	                    os.unlink(path)
301	                except OSError:
302	                    pass
303	            else:
304	                # append() is idempotent on event_id.
305	                self.audit.append(event)

307	                    path,
308	                    {"tenant_id": tenant_id,
309	                     "rules": [r.to_json() for r in rules],
310	                     "pending_event": None},
311	                )

313	    def _commit_put(self, tenant_id: str, rules: List[Rule],
314	                    event: AuditEvent, existed: bool, previous: Optional[dict]):
315	        """Write a document and its event as one logical transaction."""
316	        path = self._path_for(tenant_id)
317	        doc = {
318	            "tenant_id": tenant_id,
319	            "rules": [r.to_json() for r in rules],
320	            "pending_event": event.to_json(),
321	        }
322	        self._write_atomic(path, doc)
323	        try:
324	            self.audit.append(event)
325	        except BaseException:
326	            if not existed:
327	                try:
328	                    os.unlink(path)
329	                except OSError:
330	                    pass
331	            elif previous is not None:
332	                self._write_atomic(path, previous)
333	            raise
334	        # The durable ledger append is the commit point; clearing the marker
335	        # is post-commit housekeeping. A failure here leaves the marker for
336	        # startup recovery and must never roll the document back or fail the
337	        # request.
338	        doc["pending_event"] = None
339	        try:
340	            self._write_atomic(path, doc)
341	        except OSError:
342	            pass

344	    # -- public API --------------------------------------------------------
345	    def get(self, tenant_id: str) -> Optional[List[Rule]]:
346	        """Return the tenant's rules, or None when no document exists."""
347	        doc = self._read_doc(self._path_for(tenant_id))
348	        if doc is None:
349	            return None
350	        return doc[1]

352	    def put(self, tenant_id: str, rules: List[Rule]) -> List[Rule]:
353	        """Replace (or create) the tenant's document and audit policy_update."""
354	        with self.tenant_lock(tenant_id):
355	            path = self._path_for(tenant_id)
356	            existed = os.path.exists(path)
357	            previous = None
358	            if existed:
359	                try:
360	                    with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
361	                        previous = json.load(fh)
362	                except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
363	                    raise LedgerError(
364	                        "cannot read policy document: %s" % exc
365	                    ) from exc
366	            event = self.audit.new_event(
367	                tenant_id, audit_mod.ACTION_POLICY_UPDATE, None,
368	                audit_mod.OUTCOME_SUCCESS,
369	            )
370	            self._commit_put(tenant_id, rules, event, existed, previous)
371	        return rules
372	
373	    def delete(self, tenant_id: str) -> None:
374	        """Delete the tenant's document and audit policy_delete.
375	
376	        Tombstone sequence: write a ``.json.del`` marker carrying the event,
377	        unlink the document, append the event, then remove the marker. A crash
378	        between any two steps is repaired on the next open. If the ledger
379	        append itself fails, the original document is restored byte-for-byte
380	        and the tombstone discarded, so a failed delete never takes effect.
381	        Deleting a tenant that has no document still records the event.
382	        """
383	        with self.tenant_lock(tenant_id):
384	            path = self._path_for(tenant_id)
385	            existed = os.path.exists(path)
386	            event = self.audit.new_event(
387	                tenant_id, audit_mod.ACTION_POLICY_DELETE, None,
388	                audit_mod.OUTCOME_SUCCESS,
389	            )
390	            if not existed:
391	                self.audit.append(event)
392	                return
393	            try:
394	                with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
395	                    previous = json.load(fh)
396	            except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
397	                raise LedgerError(
398	                    "cannot read policy document: %s" % exc
399	                ) from exc
400	            tombstone = path + ".del"
401	            self._write_atomic(
402	                tombstone,
403	                {"tenant_id": tenant_id, "rules": [],
404	                 "pending_event": event.to_json()},
405	            )
406	            os.unlink(path)
407	            try:
408	                # From here on a crash is repaired from the tombstone; the
409	                # append is idempotent on event_id.
410	                self.audit.append(event)
411	            except BaseException:
412	                # The ledger write failed: roll the delete back so the
413	                # document and its event never diverge.
414	                self._write_atomic(path, previous)
415	                try:
416	                    os.unlink(tombstone)
417	                except OSError:
418	                    pass
419	                raise
420	            try:
421	                os.unlink(tombstone)
422	            except OSError:
423	                pass
424	
425	    def audit_read(self, tenant_id: str) -> None:
426	        """Record a successful policy_read (the document is never modified)."""
427	        event = self.audit.new_event(
428	            tenant_id, audit_mod.ACTION_POLICY_READ, None,
429	            audit_mod.OUTCOME_SUCCESS,
430	        )
431	        self.audit.append(event)
432	
433	    def is_allowed(self, tenant_id: str, action: str, subject: str) -> bool:
434	        """Enforce the tenant document for (subject, action).
435	
436	        No document means unrestricted. Otherwise deny wins, and an action no
437	        rule matches is denied.
438	        """
439	        rules = self.get(tenant_id)
440	        if rules is None:
441	            return True
442	        allowed = False
443	        for rule in rules:
444	            if rule.subject != subject or action not in rule.actions:
445	                continue
446	            if rule.effect == "deny":
447	                return False
448	            allowed = True
449	        return allowed

451	    # -- tenant restore hooks ---------------------------------------------
452	    def owner_of_path(self, path: str) -> Optional[str]:
453	        """Return the owning tenant_id recorded inside a policy file."""
454	        doc = self._read_doc(path)
455	        if doc is None:
456	            return None
457	        return doc[0]

459	    def write_restore_pending(
460	        self, tenant_id: str, rules: List[Rule], marker: dict
461	    ) -> None:
462	        """Atomically write a restored policy document carrying the marker.
463	
464	        Used by the RestoreCoordinator; the caller guarantees no document
465	        exists for the tenant and holds the write lock.
466	        """
467	        self._write_atomic(

469	            {
470	                "tenant_id": tenant_id,
471	                "rules": [r.to_json() for r in rules],
472	                "pending_event": marker,
473	            },
474	        )
475	
476	    def clear_restore_pending(self, tenant_id: str, rules: List[Rule]) -> None:
477	        """Rewrite a restored policy document without its pending marker."""
478	        self._write_atomic(
479	            self._path_for(tenant_id),
480	            {
481	                "tenant_id": tenant_id,
482	                "rules": [r.to_json() for r in rules],
483	                "pending_event": None,
484	            },
485	        )
486	
487	    def remove_restore_file(self, tenant_id: str) -> None:
488	        """Delete a policy document written by a restore being rolled back."""
489	        try:
490	            os.unlink(self._path_for(tenant_id))
491	        except FileNotFoundError:

1	"""KMS/HSM provider abstraction.
2	
3	Every private key is owned by a *provider*: a local software key store by
4	default, or an external KMS/HSM reached through the ``module:factory`` entry
5	point named by ``KEYMGR_PROVIDER``. The rest of the package never touches raw
6	key material when a provider is in use: it only persists the opaque
7	``provider_id`` / ``handle`` / ``encrypted_material`` triple a provider
8	returns, and asks the provider to turn a handle back into exportable material.
9	
10	Provider contract
11	-----------------
12	A provider instance exposes:
13	
14	* ``provider_id``: a non-empty string;
15	* ``capabilities``: ``{"algorithms": ["AES256", "RSA2048"],
16	  "operations": ["generate", "rotate", "import_material",
17	  "export_material", "delete"]}``;
18	* ``generate(algorithm)`` / ``rotate(algorithm)`` ->
19	  ``{"handle", "public_key", "encrypted_material"}``;
20	* ``import_material(algorithm, public_key, material)`` -> the same triple;
21	* ``export_material(handle)`` -> ``{"public_key", "encrypted_material"}``;
22	* ``delete(handle)`` -> ``None``, idempotent.
23	
24	The factory named by ``KEYMGR_PROVIDER=module:factory`` is imported lazily on
25	first use and called with no arguments. A missing module/factory, a factory
26	raising, or a returned object failing the contract all raise
27	:class:`ProviderUnavailable`; the service answers ``503`` (CLI exit ``1``) and
28	never falls back to the local provider.
29	"""
30	
31	import base64
32	import importlib
33	import json
34	import os
35	import tempfile
36	import threading
37	import uuid
38	from typing import NamedTuple, Optional
39	
40	from cryptography.exceptions import UnsupportedAlgorithm
41	from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import serialization
42	from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric import rsa
43	from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.ciphers.aead import AESGCM
44	
45	from .crypto import SUPPORTED_ALGORITHMS, generate_key

47	#: Default provider id and the id of the built-in software provider.
48	LOCAL_PROVIDER_ID = "local"
49	
50	OP_GENERATE = "generate"
51	OP_ROTATE = "rotate"
52	OP_IMPORT_MATERIAL = "import_material"
53	OP_EXPORT_MATERIAL = "export_material"
54	OP_DELETE = "delete"
55	OPERATIONS = (
56	    OP_GENERATE,
57	    OP_ROTATE,
58	    OP_IMPORT_MATERIAL,
59	    OP_EXPORT_MATERIAL,
60	    OP_DELETE,
61	)
62	
63	_DEK_NAME = "local.dek"

66	# encoding so wrapped blobs are self-describing on disk.

71	class ProviderError(Exception):

75	class ProviderUnavailable(ProviderError):
76	    """The provider cannot service the request (load/backend/handle failure).
77	
78	    Surfaced as HTTP ``503`` / CLI exit code ``1``. The message is logged
79	    server-side; clients only ever see a generic status (handles and material
80	    never leave the boundary).
81	    """

88	    offending field but never embeds the material itself.

92	class MaterialTriple(NamedTuple):
93	    """The provider-owned result of generate/rotate/import_material."""

95	    handle: str
96	    public_key: Optional[str]
97	    encrypted_material: str

108	    return base64.urlsafe_b64encode(raw).rstrip(b"=").decode("ascii")

115	def _require_triple(result, operation: str) -> MaterialTriple:
116	    """Validate a generate/rotate/import result has a handle and material."""
117	    if not isinstance(result, dict):
118	        raise ProviderUnavailable(
119	            "provider %s returned a non-object from %s"
120	            % ("external", operation)
121	        )
122	    handle = result.get("handle")
123	    material = result.get("encrypted_material")
124	    if not isinstance(handle, str) or not handle:
125	        raise ProviderUnavailable(
126	            "provider returned an empty handle from %s" % operation
127	        )
128	    if not isinstance(material, str) or not material:
129	        raise ProviderUnavailable(
130	            "provider returned empty encrypted_material from %s" % operation
131	        )
132	    public_key = result.get("public_key")
133	    if public_key is not None and not isinstance(public_key, str):
134	        raise ProviderUnavailable(
135	            "provider returned an invalid public_key from %s" % operation
136	        )
137	    return MaterialTriple(
138	        handle=handle, public_key=public_key, encrypted_material=material
139	    )

143	    """Abstract provider; concrete providers implement the five operations."""

162	    ) -> MaterialTriple:

169	        raise NotImplementedError

171	    def supports(self, algorithm: str, operation: str) -> bool:
172	        caps = getattr(self, "capabilities", {}) or {}
173	        return (

175	            and operation in caps.get("operations", ())

179	def _validate_external(obj) -> None:
180	    """Check a factory-built object satisfies the provider contract."""
181	    provider_id = getattr(obj, "provider_id", None)
182	    if not isinstance(provider_id, str) or not provider_id:
183	        raise ProviderUnavailable(
184	            "provider factory returned an object without a non-empty provider_id"
185	        )
186	    caps = getattr(obj, "capabilities", None)
187	    if not isinstance(caps, dict):
188	        raise ProviderUnavailable(
189	            "provider %r has no capabilities mapping" % provider_id
190	        )
191	    algorithms = caps.get("algorithms")
192	    operations = caps.get("operations")
193	    if not isinstance(algorithms, (list, tuple)) or not isinstance(
194	        operations, (list, tuple)
195	    ):
196	        raise ProviderUnavailable(
197	            "provider %r capabilities must list algorithms and operations"
198	            % provider_id
199	        )
200	    missing = [a for a in SUPPORTED_ALGORITHMS if a not in algorithms]
201	    if missing:
202	        raise ProviderUnavailable(
203	            "provider %r lacks required algorithms: %s"
204	            % (provider_id, ", ".join(missing))
205	        )
206	    missing_ops = [op for op in OPERATIONS if op not in operations]
207	    if missing_ops:
208	        raise ProviderUnavailable(
209	            "provider %r lacks required operations: %s"
210	            % (provider_id, ", ".join(missing_ops))
211	        )
212	    for name in OPERATIONS:
213	        if not callable(getattr(obj, name, None)):
214	            raise ProviderUnavailable(
215	                "provider %r is missing a callable %s() operation"
216	                % (provider_id, name)
217	            )
218	    configure = getattr(obj, "configure", None)
219	    if configure is not None and not callable(configure):
220	        raise ProviderUnavailable(
221	            "provider %r has a non-callable configure attribute" % provider_id
222	        )

225	class _SafeProvider:
226	    """Adapter around an external provider enforcing the error contract.
227	
228	    ProviderError subtypes pass through unchanged; any other exception the
229	    external module raises is normalized to ProviderUnavailable so a backend
230	    fault always surfaces as 503 and never as a 500 or a fallback.
231	    """
232	
233	    def __init__(self, inner) -> None:
234	        self._inner = inner
235	        self.provider_id = inner.provider_id
236	        self.capabilities = inner.capabilities

239	        try:

251	        method = getattr(self._inner, name)

253	            return method(*args)

293	    def delete(self, handle: str) -> None:
294	        # Idempotent by contract; even so, a backend fault on delete is a 503
295	        # (the caller may retry, and delete must remain idempotent).

299	class LocalProvider(KeyProvider):
300	    """Built-in software provider.
301	
302	    Raw material never lands in a key file: each generated/imported key is
303	    wrapped with AES-256-GCM under a data-encryption key kept in
304	    ``local.dek`` (0600), and only the wrapped blob plus an opaque handle is
305	    persisted. A small registry (``local-registry.json``, 0600) maps each
306	    handle to its algorithm and wrapped blob, so ``export_material(handle)``
307	    can re-derive the raw material and ``delete`` stays idempotent. The
308	    registry stores only DEK-wrapped material, never plaintext.
309	    """
310	
311	    provider_id = LOCAL_PROVIDER_ID
312	    capabilities = {
313	        "algorithms": tuple(SUPPORTED_ALGORITHMS),
314	        "operations": OPERATIONS,
315	    }
316	
317	    def __init__(self) -> None:
318	        self._lock = threading.Lock()
319	        self._data_dir: Optional[str] = None
320	        self._dek: Optional[bytes] = None
321	        self._registry: dict = {}
322	        self._configured = False
323	
324	    # -- state -------------------------------------------------------------
325	    def configure(self, data_dir: str) -> None:
326	        with self._lock:
327	            if self._configured and self._data_dir == data_dir:
328	                return
329	            os.makedirs(data_dir, exist_ok=True)
330	            self._data_dir = data_dir
331	            self._dek = self._load_or_create_dek(data_dir)
332	            self._registry = self._load_registry(data_dir)
333	            self._configured = True
334	
335	    @staticmethod
336	    def _load_or_create_dek(data_dir: str) -> bytes:
337	        path = os.path.join(data_dir, _DEK_NAME)
338	        try:
339	            with open(path, "rb") as fh:
340	                dek = fh.read()
341	            if len(dek) == 32:
342	                return dek
343	        except FileNotFoundError:
344	            pass
345	        except OSError as exc:
346	            raise ProviderUnavailable("cannot read local DEK: %s" % exc) from exc
347	        dek = os.urandom(32)
348	        try:
349	            fd = os.open(path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL, 0o600)
350	            try:
351	                os.write(fd, dek)
352	                os.fsync(fd)
353	            finally:
354	                os.close(fd)
355	        except FileExistsError:
356	            with open(path, "rb") as fh:
357	                dek = fh.read()
358	        except OSError as exc:
359	            raise ProviderUnavailable("cannot write local DEK: %s" % exc) from exc
360	        if len(dek) != 32:
361	            raise ProviderUnavailable("local DEK file is corrupt")
362	        return dek

364	    @staticmethod
365	    def _load_registry(data_dir: str) -> dict:
366	        path = os.path.join(data_dir, _REGISTRY_NAME)
367	        try:
368	            with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
369	                data = json.load(fh)
370	        except FileNotFoundError:
371	            return {}
372	        except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
373	            raise ProviderUnavailable(
374	                "cannot read local handle registry: %s" % exc
375	            ) from exc
376	        if not isinstance(data, dict):
377	            raise ProviderUnavailable("local handle registry is corrupt")
378	        return data

380	    def _persist_registry_locked(self) -> None:
381	        path = os.path.join(self._data_dir, _REGISTRY_NAME)
382	        fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=self._data_dir, suffix=".tmp")
383	        try:
384	            with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
385	                json.dump(self._registry, fh)
386	                fh.flush()
387	                os.fsync(fh.fileno())
388	            os.chmod(tmp_path, 0o600)
389	            os.replace(tmp_path, path)
390	        except BaseException:
391	            try:

284	    imported material (400) is a durable terminal -- the safe response is
285	    staged, one rejected event named after the operation_id is appended
286	    (rotate projects the request key_id, import the in-bundle key_id, restore
287	    null), and the op is finished, so an HTTP/CLI cross-retry replays exactly
288	    this result and the event is never duplicated. Raises OSError/LedgerError
289	    if that persistence itself fails (the caller finalizes failed(500)).
290	    """

295	    if kind == "batch_rotate":
296	        action = audit_mod.ACTION_BATCH_ROTATE
297	    elif kind == "rotate":
298	        action = audit_mod.ACTION_ROTATE
299	    else:
300	        action = audit_mod.ACTION_IMPORT
301	    audit_key_id = (
302	        None if kind in ("restore", "batch_rotate")
303	        else (
304	            details.get("key_id")
305	            if is_valid_key_id(details.get("key_id"))
306	            else None
307	        )
308	    )
309	    op_store.stage_terminal(
310	        operation,
311	        http_status,
312	        body,
313	        audit={
314	            "action": action,
315	            "outcome": audit_mod.OUTCOME_REJECTED,
316	            "tenant_id": operation.tenant_id,
317	            "key_id": audit_key_id,
318	        },
319	    )

321	        operation.tenant_id, audit_key_id, action,
322	        audit_mod.OUTCOME_REJECTED, event_id=op_id,
323	    )

403	def _run_owned_attempt(op_store, store, artifact_store, executor, operation,
404	                       blocking, takeover=False) -> int:
405	    """Run one attempt under its mirror + cross-process claim.
406	
407	    Used by the binding winner (takeover=False) and by an identical retry that
408	    takes a stranded pending attempt over (takeover=True). A mirror claim/
409	    creation failure leaves the operation pending and returns the 500/503 exit
410	    code without calling a provider or writing any key/handle/audit.
411	    """
412	    op_id = operation.operation_id
413	    if artifact_store is None:
414	        return _idempotent_run_body(
415	            op_store, store, None, executor, operation, op_id, None
416	        )
417	    from .artifacts import (
418	        ArtifactAlreadyTerminal,
419	        ArtifactStrandUnavailable,
420	    )
421	
422	    attempt_cm = artifact_store.attempt(
423	        operation, blocking, takeover=takeover,
424	        operation_store=op_store if takeover else None,
425	    )
426	    try:
427	        mirror = attempt_cm.__enter__()
428	    except ArtifactAlreadyTerminal as already:
429	        # The owner reached a terminal while the claim was taken: replay its
430	        # fresh stored result verbatim, execute nothing.
431	        return _emit_operation_result(
432	            already.record.http_status, already.record.response
433	        )
434	    except ArtifactStrandUnavailable as exc:
435	        return _emit_operation_result(
436	            exc.http_status, _strand_unavailable_body(op_id)
437	        )
438	    except BlockingIOError:
439	        raise
440	    try:
441	        return _idempotent_run_body(
442	            op_store, store, artifact_store, executor,
443	            operation, op_id, mirror,
444	        )
445	    except ArtifactStrandUnavailable as exc:
446	        # The mirror could not be described/tied in before the first provider
447	        # call: keep the operation pending for a same-id retry.
448	        return _emit_operation_result(
449	            exc.http_status, _strand_unavailable_body(op_id)
450	        )
451	    finally:
452	        attempt_cm.__exit__(None, None, None)

455	def idempotent_run(op_store, store, path, tenant_id, operator, body, key,
456	                   validator, executor, decoder=None, artifact_store=None):
457	    """CLI counterpart of the HTTP idempotency guard.
458	
459	    Returns a process exit code. ``validator()`` runs cheap side-effect-free
460	    request checks *before* the binding lookup and returns None on success or
461	    an ``(exit_code, message)`` refusal (a refusal is never audited and never
462	    consumes the key). ``decoder`` (when given) performs the side-effect-free
463	    but expensive validation -- bundle decryption -- *after* an already-bound
464	    key has been replayed/conflicted but *before* a new key is bound, so a
465	    wrong passphrase neither masks a replay nor consumes the key.
466	    ``executor(operation, mirror) -> (http_status, body)`` runs once for a new
467	    binding and may raise ProviderInvalidMaterial / ProviderUnavailable /
468	    LedgerError / LockTimeout.
469	    """
470	    if _idem_key_error(key):
471	        return 2
472	    normalized = operations_mod.normalize_body(body)
473	
474	    refusal = validator()
475	    if refusal is not None:
476	        code, message = refusal
477	        return _fail(message, code)
478	
479	    # An already-bound key replays/conflicts before the expensive decoder
480	    # (bundle decryption), so a bad passphrase on a retry never masks a
481	    # replay or consumes the key.
482	    peek = op_store.peek(tenant_id, operator, path, normalized, key)
483	    existing = _idem_serve_existing(op_store, peek.kind, peek.record)
484	    if existing is not None:
485	        return existing
486	
487	    if decoder is not None:
488	        refusal = decoder()
489	        if refusal is not None:
490	            code, message = refusal
491	            return _fail(message, code)
492	
493	    # begin() is authoritative for the bind (another process may have won
494	    # between the peek and here).
495	    begin = op_store.begin(tenant_id, operator, path, normalized, key)
496	    if begin.kind == "conflict":
497	        return _idem_serve_existing(op_store, "conflict", begin.record)
498	    if begin.kind == "replay":
499	        if begin.record.is_terminal():
500	            return _idem_serve_existing(op_store, "replay", begin.record)
501	        # Still pending: take a stranded attempt over immediately; if a live
502	        # owner (thread or process) holds the claim, wait for its terminal.
503	        if artifact_store is not None:
504	            try:
505	                return _run_owned_attempt(
506	                    op_store, store, artifact_store, executor,
507	                    begin.record, blocking=False, takeover=True,
508	                )
509	            except BlockingIOError:
510	                return _idem_wait_then_serve(op_store, begin.record)
511	        return _idem_wait_then_serve(op_store, begin.record)
512	
513	    operation = begin.record
514	    return _run_owned_attempt(
515	        op_store, store, artifact_store, executor, operation,
516	        blocking=True, takeover=False,
517	    )
518

520	def _idempotent_run_body(op_store, store, artifact_store, executor, operation,
521	                         op_id, mirror):
522	    from .artifacts import ArtifactStrandUnavailable
523	
524	    try:
525	        http_status, resp = executor(operation, mirror)
526	    except ArtifactStrandUnavailable as exc:
527	        # The mirror could not be described/tied in before the first provider
528	        # call: nothing committed, keep the operation pending for a same-id
529	        # retry (exit 1).
530	        return _emit_operation_result(
531	            exc.http_status, _strand_unavailable_body(op_id)
532	        )
533	    except LockTimeout:
534	        body_err = {
535	            "error": "operation timed out waiting for a lock",
536	            "operation_id": op_id,
537	        }
538	        op_store.finish(
539	            operation, operations_mod.STATUS_TIMED_OUT, 503, body_err
540	        )
541	        return _emit_operation_result(503, body_err)
542	    except ProviderInvalidMaterial as exc:
543	        try:
544	            http_status, body_err = _provider_terminal(
545	                op_store, store, operation, 400, str(exc)
546	            )
547	            return _emit_operation_result(http_status, body_err)
548	        except (OSError, LedgerError) as persist_exc:
549	            body_err = {
550	                "error": "audit ledger failure: %s" % persist_exc,
551	                "operation_id": op_id,
552	            }
553	            op_store.finish(
554	                operation, operations_mod.STATUS_FAILED, 500, body_err
555	            )
556	            return _emit_operation_result(500, body_err)
557	    except ProviderUnavailable:
558	        try:
559	            http_status, body_err = _provider_terminal(
560	                op_store, store, operation, 503,
561	                "key management provider is unavailable",
562	            )
563	            return _emit_operation_result(http_status, body_err)
564	        except (OSError, LedgerError) as persist_exc:
565	            body_err = {
566	                "error": "audit ledger failure: %s" % persist_exc,
567	                "operation_id": op_id,
568	            }
569	            op_store.finish(
570	                operation, operations_mod.STATUS_FAILED, 500, body_err
571	            )
572	            return _emit_operation_result(500, body_err)
573	    except OSError as exc:
574	        # A pre-commit staging/write failure happened before the commit-point
575	        # append: file and handles were rolled back, nothing committed.
576	        # Finalize failed(500).
577	        body_err = {
578	            "error": "audit ledger failure: %s" % exc,
579	            "operation_id": op_id,
580	        }
581	        op_store.finish(operation, operations_mod.STATUS_FAILED, 500, body_err)
582	        return _emit_operation_result(500, body_err)
583	    except LedgerError as exc:
584	        body_err = {
585	            "error": "audit ledger failure: %s" % exc,
586	            "operation_id": op_id,
587	        }
588	        op_store.finish(operation, operations_mod.STATUS_FAILED, 500, body_err)
589	        return _emit_operation_result(500, body_err)
590	    resp = dict(resp)
591	    resp["operation_id"] = op_id
592	    state = operations_mod.state_for_http_status(http_status)
593	    op_store.finish(operation, state, http_status, resp)
594	    if artifact_store is not None and mirror is not None:
595	        # Committed: verified ownership then dropped; uncommitted: dropped
596	        # only once every rollback artifact is gone. A mirror that cannot be
597	        # verified survives for the next startup.
598	        artifact_store.after_terminal(mirror)
599	    return _emit_operation_result(http_status, resp)
